name: fidchell

attributes.attribute: the name refers to wood wisdom

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Fidchell is an ancient Irish game. It resembled the game cribbage, with pegs moved about a board. The name refers to wood wisdom, so the pegs likely were cut of wood. Fidchell shared strategy with chess, where a player took the pieces of an opponent. No game board has been found. The game appears often in mythological story. The king of the Otherworld, Midir, wagered against Eochaid Airem, king of Tara, with queen Etain as the prize.
